source: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR) as it applies to AI, with EDPB Opinion 28/2024.
disclaimer: This repository is general information to help you understand and organize work on AI governance frameworks. It is not legal advice and does not guarantee compliance, certification or any regulatory outcome. Requirements are summarized in our own words; always check the official texts and get qualified advice for your situation.

requirements.title: Data protection principles for AI
requirements.summary: Apply lawfulness, fairness, transparency, purpose limitation, minimization, accuracy, storage limitation, security and accountability to training and use.

requirements.title: Lawful basis
requirements.summary: Identify a lawful basis for each processing purpose in development and deployment; legitimate interest needs a documented three-step test (EDPB Opinion 28/2024).
requirements.evidence: Legitimate interest assessments; lawful basis register.

requirements.title: Special category data
requirements.summary: Process sensitive data only under an Article 9(2) condition; see also AI Act Art. 4a for bias correction.

requirements.title: Transparency to individuals
requirements.summary: Tell people how their data is used for AI, including sources when not collected from them.

requirements.title: Data subject rights
requirements.summary: Handle access, rectification, erasure and objection requests, including for training data where applicable.

requirements.title: Automated decision-making
requirements.summary: Respect limits on solely automated decisions with legal or similar effects; offer human intervention and the right to contest.

requirements.title: Data protection by design and default
requirements.summary: Build privacy into AI design: minimization, pseudonymization, access limits.

requirements.title: Processors
requirements.summary: Contracts with AI vendors processing personal data on your behalf.

requirements.title: Security
requirements.summary: Appropriate security for AI data and models, including AI-specific attacks.

requirements.title: Data protection impact assessment
requirements.summary: Run a DPIA for high-risk AI processing; can be linked to the AI Act FRIA.

requirements.title: Anonymity of AI models
requirements.summary: Do not assume a model trained on personal data is anonymous; assess case by case.
